schema.id: REQ-ID, stable, cited in every finding
schema.section: section of SP 800-63B-4 the quote is taken from
schema.quote: verbatim substring of reference_text (markdown emphasis stripped); checks/verify_citations.py enforces this
schema.level: normative level as written by NIST: SHALL | SHALL NOT | SHOULD | SHOULD NOT. MAY/NEED NOT statements are never controls
schema.condition: null, or a factual applicability predicate: a verifier63.yaml field (aal, password_usage) or an observable fact about the implementation (e.g. keyed_hash_or_encryption_step_present). A condition never references another control's PASS/FAIL result. condition true -> audit; condition false -> NOT APPLICABLE; condition unknown from supplied evidence -> EVIDENCE REQUIRED
schema.status_values: PASS | FAIL | EVIDENCE REQUIRED | NOT APPLICABLE (status is recorded on the finding, not here)
schema.detection_strategy: MECHANICAL_FIRST (checks/mechanical.ts implements mechanical_check; unresolved patterns downgrade to SEMANTIC) | SEMANTIC_ONLY
schema.mechanical_check: name of the check in checks/mechanical.ts (MECHANICAL_FIRST only)
schema.level_source: optional: verbatim sentence in the same section that carries the normative keyword when `quote` is a list item governed by an introducing sentence
schema.notes: how the auditor evaluates it; not normative

conformance_severity.note: Derived by Verifier63 from normative level. NIST supplies the level, not a risk rating.

controls.quote: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL require passwords that are used as a single-factor authentication mechanism to be a minimum of 15 characters in length.
controls.notes: Minimum enforced length must be >= 15 when the password is the only factor.

controls.quote: Verifiers and CSPs MAY allow passwords that are only used as part of multi-factor authentication processes to be shorter but SHALL require them to be a minimum of eight characters in length.
controls.notes: Minimum enforced length must be >= 8 when the password is one factor of MFA.

controls.quote: Verifiers and CSPs SHOULD permit a maximum password length of at least 64 characters.
controls.notes: A maximum below 64 fails. No maximum passes.

controls.quote: Verifiers SHALL request the password to be provided in full (not a subset of it)
controls.notes: Fails if the login flow asks for selected characters/positions of the password.

controls.quote: SHALL verify the entire submitted password (e.g., not truncate it).
controls.notes: Fails if the password is sliced/substringed before hashing or comparison. Note bcrypt truncates input at 72 bytes; flag as SEMANTIC when bcrypt is used without a max length <= 72.

controls.quote: Verifiers and CSPs SHOULD accept all printing ASCII [RFC20] characters and the space character in passwords.
controls.notes: Fails if a validator rejects any printing ASCII character or the space, or strips spaces.

controls.quote: Verifiers and CSPs SHOULD accept Unicode [ISO/ISC 10646] characters in passwords.
controls.notes: Fails if a validator restricts input to an ASCII-only character class.

controls.quote: Each Unicode code point SHALL be counted as a single character when evaluating password length.
controls.notes: JavaScript String.length counts UTF-16 code units, not code points; a length check using .length on a Unicode-accepting validator is a deviation for astral characters. Quote the length expression.

controls.quote: If Unicode characters are accepted in passwords, the verifier SHOULD apply the normalization process for stabilized strings using the Normalization Form Canonical Composition (NFC) normalization
controls.notes: Applies only when Unicode is accepted. Passes if String.prototype.normalize('NFC') (or equivalent) is applied before hashing.

controls.quote: Subscribers choosing passwords that contain Unicode characters SHOULD be advised that some endpoints may represent some characters differently
controls.notes: UI guidance text; usually EVIDENCE REQUIRED when only server code is supplied.

controls.quote: When processing a request to establish or change a password, verifiers SHALL compare the prospective secret against a blocklist that contains known commonly used, expected, or compromised passwords.
controls.notes: Look for a blocklist / breach-corpus / HIBP check on the create and change paths.

controls.quote: The entire password SHALL be subject to comparison, not substrings or words that might be contained therein.
controls.notes: Fails if the blocklist check matches substrings or tokenized words rather than the whole password.

controls.quote: If the chosen password is found on the blocklist, the CSP SHALL require the subscriber to select a different secret
controls.notes: A blocklist hit must reject, not warn.

controls.quote: and SHALL provide the reason for rejection.
controls.notes: The rejection response must state that the password was found on a blocklist of common/compromised passwords.

controls.quote: the blocklist SHOULD be of sufficient size to prevent subscribers from choosing passwords that attackers are likely to guess before reaching the attempt limit.
controls.notes: Usually EVIDENCE REQUIRED unless the list or its source is supplied.

controls.quote: Verifiers SHALL offer guidance to the subscriber to help the subscriber choose a strong password.
controls.notes: Guidance text at password creation; usually EVIDENCE REQUIRED when only server code is supplied.

controls.quote: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL NOT impose other composition rules (e.g., requiring mixtures of different character types) for passwords.
controls.notes: A character-class check whose result reaches a rejection path (throw, return false, error push) is enforcement. The same check feeding only a logger, metric or strength meter is observation and passes.

controls.quote: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL NOT require subscribers to change passwords periodically.
controls.notes: Fails on any age-based expiry (maxAge, rotation interval, passwordExpiresAt) applied to passwords.

controls.quote: However, verifiers SHALL force a change if there is evidence that the authenticator has been compromised.
controls.notes: Look for a compromised/must-reset flag that forces a change on next login.

controls.quote: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL NOT permit the subscriber to store a hint (e.g., a reminder of how the password was created) that is accessible to an unauthenticated claimant.
controls.notes: Fails if a password hint is stored and returned on the login or reset path before authentication.

controls.quote: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL NOT prompt subscribers to use knowledge-based authentication (KBA) (e.g., “What was the name of your first pet?”) or security questions when choosing passwords.
controls.notes: Fails if security questions are collected as part of password creation.

controls.quote: Verifiers SHALL allow the use of password managers and autofill functionality.
controls.notes: Fails on autocomplete="off" on password fields or scripts that block autofill. EVIDENCE REQUIRED when no client code is supplied.

controls.quote: Verifiers SHOULD permit claimants to use the “paste” function when entering a password
controls.notes: Fails on onPaste handlers that preventDefault on password fields. EVIDENCE REQUIRED when no client code is supplied.

controls.quote: the verifier SHOULD offer an option to display the password — rather than a series of dots or asterisks — while it is entered and until it is submitted to the verifier.
controls.notes: Show/hide password toggle. EVIDENCE REQUIRED when no client code is supplied.

controls.quote: Verifiers and CSPs SHALL use approved encryption and an authenticated protected channel when requesting passwords.
controls.notes: TLS termination is normally outside application code; EVIDENCE REQUIRED unless server/TLS config is supplied. Fails if a password is accepted over a plain http listener in the supplied code.

controls.quote: Verifiers SHALL store passwords in a form that is resistant to offline attacks.
controls.notes: Plaintext, reversible encryption, or an unsalted fast hash fails.

controls.quote: Passwords SHALL be salted and hashed using a suitable password hashing scheme.
controls.notes: argon2 / scrypt / bcrypt / PBKDF2 with a salt passes. Plain createHash (md5, sha1, sha256) on the password, or no hashing, fails.

controls.quote: The chosen cost factor SHOULD be as high as practical without negatively impacting verifier performance.
controls.notes: Quote the cost / rounds / memory parameters. Below the library's current default is a deviation.

controls.quote: It SHOULD be increased over time to account for increases in computing performance.
controls.notes: Look for a rehash-on-login or versioned cost factor; otherwise EVIDENCE REQUIRED.

controls.quote: An approved password hashing scheme published in the latest revision of [SP800-132] or updated NIST guidelines on password hashing schemes SHOULD be used.
controls.notes: The current final SP 800-132 (December 2010) specifies PBKDF2. Argon2 or scrypt without an updated NIST guideline qualifying them is Status FAIL, Level SHOULD, Severity LOW, with the note: this is a deviation from this NIST recommendation; it is not a finding that Argon2/scrypt is insecure. PBKDF2 with a salt and a documented iteration count passes.

controls.quote: The chosen output length of the password verifier, excluding the salt and versioning information, SHOULD be the same as the length of the underlying password hashing scheme output.
controls.notes: Fails if the hash output is truncated before storage.

controls.quote: The salt SHALL be at least 32 bits in length
controls.notes: Library defaults (bcrypt 128-bit, argon2 128-bit, scrypt user-supplied) pass when the default is used; quote the salt generation if explicit.

controls.quote: and chosen to minimize salt value collisions among stored hashes (i.e., to prevent multiple subscriber accounts from having the same hashed password).
controls.level_source: The salt SHALL be at least 32 bits in length and chosen to minimize salt value collisions among stored hashes
controls.notes: Fails on a fixed, per-application, or low-entropy salt.

controls.quote: Both the salt value and the resulting hash SHALL be stored for each password.
controls.notes: Passes when the scheme embeds the salt in its output string (bcrypt, argon2 PHC format) or the salt column is stored.

controls.quote: A reference to the password hashing scheme used, including the cost factor, SHOULD be stored for each password to allow migration to new algorithms and work factors.
controls.notes: PHC / modular crypt format strings satisfy this; a bare hex digest does not.

controls.quote: In addition, verifiers SHOULD perform an additional iteration of a keyed hashing or encryption operation using a secret key known only to the verifier.
controls.notes: Pepper / HMAC step. Absence is a LOW deviation, not a conformance failure.

controls.quote: If used, this key value SHALL be generated by an approved random bit generator, as described in Sec. 3.2.12.
controls.notes: Applies only if a keyed step is implemented. Usually EVIDENCE REQUIRED (key provisioning is outside code).

controls.quote: The secret key value SHALL be stored separately from the hashed passwords.
controls.notes: Applies only if a keyed step is implemented. Fails if the key sits in the same table/row as the hashes.

controls.quote: It SHOULD be stored and used within a hardware-protected area, such as a hardware security module or trusted execution environment (TEE)
controls.notes: Applies only if a keyed step is implemented. Almost always EVIDENCE REQUIRED.

controls.quote: Verifiers SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the number of failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber account, as described in Sec. 3.2.2.
controls.notes: Some per-account throttle must exist in the supplied code or supplied infra config. Same obligation as §3.2.2 "the verifier SHALL implement controls to protect against online guessing attacks".

controls.quote: the verifier SHALL limit consecutive failed authentication attempts using a specific authenticator on a single subscriber account to no more than 100 by disabling that authenticator.
controls.notes: A per-account failed-attempt counter compared against a threshold <= 100 that disables the password passes. Threshold > 100, per-IP-only limiting, or no counter fails.

controls.quote: If more than one authenticator is involved with an excessive number of authentication attempts (e.g., single-factor cryptographic authenticator and centrally verified password), both authenticators SHALL be disabled.
controls.notes: NIST's trigger is more than one authenticator being involved in an excessive number of attempts; the auditor establishes whether a second authenticator exists in the supplied code, then whether its lockout path disables both.

controls.quote: Authenticators that have been disabled SHALL be required to rebind to the subscriber account, as described in Sec. 4.1, to be usable in the future.
controls.notes: A time-based auto-unlock without rebinding (e.g., reset the password) is a deviation; quote the unlock path.

controls.quote: When the subscriber successfully authenticates, the verifier SHOULD disregard any previous failed attempts for the authenticators used in the successful authentication.
controls.notes: Counter reset on success. §3.2.2 states the same observable obligation twice ("disregard any previous failed attempts" / "reset the retry count"); the second sentence is mapped to this control in OUT-OF-SCOPE.md and not scored twice.

controls.quote: If this is provided, the maximum AAL of the authenticator being reset SHALL not exceed the AAL of the session from which it is being reset.
controls.notes: Applies only if a reset is provided. Usually EVIDENCE REQUIRED in single-AAL applications.

controls.quote: A session secret SHALL be shared between the subscriber’s software and the accessed service.
controls.notes: A session identifier or token must exist.

controls.quote: The secret SHALL be directly presented by the subscriber’s software, or possession of the secret SHALL be proven using a cryptographic mechanism.
controls.notes: Cookie or bearer presentation satisfies this.

controls.quote: The continuity of authenticated sessions SHALL be based on the possession of a session secret that is issued by the session host at the time of authentication and optionally refreshed during the session.
controls.notes: Fails if continuity relies on re-sent credentials or client-asserted identity.

controls.quote: Session secrets that are used as bearer tokens for session management SHOULD NOT be persistent (i.e., retained across a restart of the associated application or a reboot of the host device)
controls.notes: A long-lived persistent session cookie is a deviation; see COOK-04 for expiry.

controls.quote: Cookies and similar “remember my browser” features SHALL NOT be used instead of authentication except as provided for reauthentication at AAL2 in Sec. 2.2.3 when the inactivity limit has been exceeded but the time limit has not.
controls.notes: "Remember me" that skips authentication after the overall timeout fails.

controls.quote: However, RPs and CSPs SHALL ensure that the session lifetime limits described in Sec. 2.2.3 are enforced even when a knowledge of the session secret is demonstrated.
controls.notes: Timeouts apply regardless of proof-of-possession technology. Evidence is the REAUTH results.

controls.quote: The secret used for session binding SHALL be generated by the session host in direct response to an authentication event.
controls.notes: Session must be (re)generated at login, not reused from the pre-authentication session (session fixation).

controls.quote: A session SHOULD inherit the AAL properties of the authentication event that triggered its creation.
controls.notes: Usually EVIDENCE REQUIRED in single-AAL applications.

controls.quote: A session MAY be considered at a lower AAL than the authentication event but SHALL NOT be considered at a higher AAL than the authentication event.
controls.notes: Usually EVIDENCE REQUIRED in single-AAL applications.

controls.quote: Secrets are established during or immediately following authentication.
controls.level_source: The secrets used for session binding SHALL meet all of the following requirements:
controls.notes: Item 1 of the list introduced by "The secrets used for session binding SHALL meet all of the following requirements". Same evidence as SESS-07.

controls.quote: Secrets are established using input from an approved random bit generator, as described in Sec. 3.2.12, and are at least 64 bits in length.
controls.level_source: The secrets used for session binding SHALL meet all of the following requirements:
controls.notes: Item 2 of the SHALL list. crypto.randomBytes(n>=8) / randomUUID / a session library documented to use a CSPRNG passes; Math.random, Date.now, incrementing ids fail.

controls.quote: Secrets are erased or invalidated by the session subject when the subscriber logs out.
controls.level_source: The secrets used for session binding SHALL meet all of the following requirements:
controls.notes: Item 3 of the SHALL list. Logout must destroy the server-side session / invalidate the token, not just clear the cookie.

controls.quote: Secrets are either transferred from the session host to the RP or CSP via an authenticated protected channel or derived from keys that are established as part of establishing a valid, mutually authenticated protected channel.
controls.level_source: The secrets used for session binding SHALL meet all of the following requirements:
controls.notes: Item 4 of the SHALL list. TLS; usually EVIDENCE REQUIRED with COOK-01 as partial evidence.

controls.quote: Secrets will time out and are not accepted after the times specified in Sec. 2.1.3, Sec. 2.2.3, and Sec. 2.3.3, as appropriate for the AAL.
controls.level_source: The secrets used for session binding SHALL meet all of the following requirements:
controls.notes: Item 5 of the SHALL list. Evidence is the REAUTH-02..07 results; fails if the server accepts a secret past the declared limits.

controls.quote: Secrets are unavailable to intermediaries between the host and the subscriber’s endpoint.
controls.level_source: The secrets used for session binding SHALL meet all of the following requirements:
controls.notes: Item 6 of the SHALL list. Usually EVIDENCE REQUIRED (proxy/CDN configuration).

controls.quote: the secrets used for session binding SHOULD be erased on the subscriber endpoint when they log out or when the secret is deemed to have expired.
controls.notes: Logout should clear the cookie / client storage in addition to SESS-12.

controls.quote: They SHOULD NOT be placed in insecure locations (e.g., HTML5 Local Storage) due to the potential exposure of local storage to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.
controls.notes: Fails if a session token is written to localStorage / sessionStorage in supplied client code.

controls.quote: Following authentication, authenticated sessions SHALL NOT fall back to an insecure transport (e.g., from https to http).
controls.notes: Secure cookie flag (COOK-01) plus HSTS / https redirect are the evidence; fails if an authenticated route is served over http in the supplied code.

controls.quote: POST/PUT content SHALL contain a session identifier
controls.notes: State-changing requests must carry a session-bound identifier in their content (e.g., a CSRF token field or header derived from the session). Alternative CSRF defenses (SameSite, Origin checks) may be reported as context but do not satisfy this control unless the supplied implementation satisfies the cited NIST requirement.

controls.quote: that the RP SHALL verify to protect against cross-site request forgery (CSRF).
controls.notes: The server must verify the identifier carried per SESS-19 on every POST/PUT. Same evidence boundary as SESS-19: alternative defenses are context, not satisfaction.

controls.quote: Sessions SHOULD provide a readily accessible mechanism for subscribers to terminate (i.e., log off) their session when their interaction is complete.
controls.notes: A logout route/endpoint must exist.

controls.quote: SHALL be tagged to be accessible only on secure (i.e., HTTPS) sessions.
controls.notes: secure: true (or Secure attribute) on the session cookie.

controls.quote: SHALL be accessible to the minimum practical hostnames and paths.
controls.notes: Fails on a Domain attribute set to a parent domain, or a Path broader than the application needs. Judgment required; the checker reports the values.

controls.quote: SHOULD be tagged as inaccessible via JavaScript (i.e., HttpOnly).
controls.notes: httpOnly: true.

controls.quote: SHOULD be tagged to expire at or soon after the session’s validity period.
controls.notes: maxAge / expires at or near the declared overall timeout. A cookie lifetime far beyond the overall timeout is a deviation; a session cookie (no maxAge) passes.

controls.quote: This requirement is intended to limit the accumulation of cookies but SHALL NOT be relied upon to enforce session timeouts.
controls.notes: Server-side expiry must exist independently of cookie expiry (see REAUTH-02).

controls.quote: SHOULD have the “__Host-“ prefix and set “Path=/”.
controls.notes: Cookie name begins with __Host- and path is "/".

controls.quote: SHOULD set “SameSite=Lax” or “SameSite=Strict”.
controls.notes: sameSite: 'lax' or 'strict'. 'none' or unset fails.

controls.quote: SHOULD contain only an opaque string (e.g., a session identifier)
controls.notes: A random id or an encrypted/opaque token passes; a readable JSON/JWT with claims is a deviation.

controls.quote: and SHALL NOT contain cleartext personal information.
controls.notes: Fails if email, name, or other PII is readable in the cookie value (e.g., unencrypted JWT claims).

controls.quote: The periodic reauthentication of sessions SHALL be performed to confirm the subscriber’s continued presence at an authenticated session
controls.notes: Some session expiry with a forced re-login must exist; evidence is REAUTH-02.

controls.quote: A definite reauthentication overall timeout SHALL be established
controls.notes: Same sentence appears in 2.1.3 and 2.2.3. An absolute session lifetime must be configured server-side. Rolling-only expiry with no absolute cap fails.

controls.quote: which SHOULD be no more than 30 days at AAL1.
controls.notes: Overall timeout <= 30 days.

controls.quote: which SHOULD be no more than 24 hours at AAL2.
controls.notes: Overall timeout <= 24 hours.

controls.quote: The inactivity timeout SHOULD be no more than 1 hour.
controls.notes: Inactivity (idle) timeout <= 1 hour.

controls.quote: At AAL3, the overall timeout for reauthentication SHALL be no more than 12 hours.
controls.notes: Overall timeout <= 12 hours.

controls.quote: The inactivity timeout SHOULD be no more than 15 minutes.
controls.notes: Inactivity (idle) timeout <= 15 minutes.

controls.quote: When either timeout expires, the session SHALL be terminated.
controls.notes: Expiry must be enforced server-side, not only by cookie expiry (see COOK-05).

controls.quote: Session activity SHALL reset the inactivity timeout
controls.notes: Rolling idle timeout. Applies when an inactivity timeout is implemented (required at AAL2/AAL3 as SHOULD, optional at AAL1).

controls.quote: successful reauthentication during a session SHALL reset both timeouts.
controls.notes: Re-login must issue a fresh absolute lifetime.
